name: Complaint Handling Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's formal policy governing the handling, investigation, and resolution of customer complaints. The policy is owned by the Head of Customer Service and applies to all staff and customers. It is mandated by FCA COBS Part 2 and the FCA Handbook.
context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS Part 2 (Complaints), FCA Handbook

name: FCA COBS Part 2 (Complaints)
description: The Financial Conduct Authority's Conduct of Business sourcebook Part 2, which sets out the regulatory requirements for complaint handling by authorised firms. This regulation mandates FirstUK Bank's complaint handling obligations.
context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS Part 2 (Complaints), FCA Handbook

name: FCA Handbook
description: The Financial Conduct Authority's comprehensive rulebook and guidance documentation that governs the conduct of authorised financial services firms, including complaint handling requirements.
context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS Part 2 (Complaints), FCA Handbook

name: Head of Customer Service
description: The senior role responsible for owning and overseeing the Complaint Handling Policy at FirstUK Bank. This role is accountable for the policy's implementation, maintenance, and compliance with FCA requirements.

name: Customer Service Department
description: The department within FirstUK Bank responsible for managing and implementing the Complaint Handling Policy. This department is the primary owner of complaint handling operations and procedures.

name: All Staff
description: All employees of FirstUK Bank are identified as an audience for the Complaint Handling Policy, indicating that all staff have obligations and responsibilities under this policy.

name: Customer
description: Customers of FirstUK Bank who are identified as an audience for the Complaint Handling Policy. Customers have rights to lodge complaints and receive fair treatment under this policy.

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The UK financial regulator identified as an audience for FirstUK Bank's Complaint Handling Policy. The FCA sets the regulatory requirements that this policy must comply with and oversees the bank's complaint handling practices.
context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS Part 2 (Complaints), FCA Handbook

name: Policy Version 3.0
description: The current governing policy document effective 2026-06-01 that supersedes Version 2.0. This version resolves internal inconsistencies between the Escalation Matrix and Compensation Framework sections by aligning approval thresholds across both sections.
context: This policy (Version 3.0, effective 2026-06-01) supersedes and replaces Version 2.0 (effective 2026-01-15) in full.
The revision was made to resolve an internal inconsistency identified between those two sections in Version 2.0

name: Policy Version 2.0
description: The superseded policy document that was effective from 2026-01-15 until replaced by Version 3.0 on 2026-06-01. This version contained conflicting thresholds between the Escalation Matrix and Compensation Framework sections.
context: the Escalation Matrix and Compensation Framework tables specified different Manager/Director approval boundaries for the same decisions

name: Escalation Matrix Threshold Alignment
description: The requirement that escalation decisions follow a unified set of Manager/Director approval boundaries. This provision was revised in Version 3.0 to eliminate the conflicting thresholds that existed in Version 2.0.
context: The prior version's Escalation Matrix and Compensation Framework thresholds no longer apply
this version aligns both sections on a single set of thresholds

name: Compensation Framework Threshold Alignment
description: The requirement that compensation decisions follow a unified set of Manager/Director approval boundaries. This provision was revised in Version 3.0 to eliminate the conflicting thresholds that existed in Version 2.0.
context: The prior version's Escalation Matrix and Compensation Framework thresholds no longer apply
this version aligns both sections on a single set of thresholds

name: Customer Complaints Handling Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's formal policy establishing procedures for receipt, investigation, resolution, and regulatory reporting of customer complaints in accordance with FCA requirements. The policy commits the bank to fair and efficient complaint handling.
context: FirstUK Bank is committed to handling customer complaints fairly, efficiently, and in accordance with FCA requirements.
This policy establishes procedures for complaint receipt, investigation, resolution, and regulatory reporting.

name: Financial Conduct Authority Requirements
description: The regulatory framework issued by the Financial Conduct Authority that governs customer complaint handling procedures, including receipt, investigation, resolution, and reporting obligations for FirstUK Bank.
context: FirstUK Bank is committed to handling customer complaints fairly, efficiently, and in accordance with FCA requirements.

name: Complaint Handling Risk
description: The risk of inadequate, unfair, or inefficient handling of customer complaints, which could result in regulatory breach, reputational damage, or customer detriment. This policy is designed to mitigate such risks through structured procedures.
context: FirstUK Bank is committed to handling customer complaints fairly, efficiently, and in accordance with FCA requirements.
This policy establishes procedures for complaint receipt, investigation, resolution, and regulatory reporting.

name: Customer
description: A natural person who submits a complaint to FirstUK Bank regarding its products, services, or conduct, and is the subject of the complaint handling procedures defined in this policy.
context: FirstUK Bank is committed to handling customer complaints fairly, efficiently, and in accordance with FCA requirements.
This policy establishes procedures for complaint receipt, investigation, resolution, and regulatory reporting.

name: Complaint Handling Policy
description: A formal policy establishing procedures for acknowledging, investigating, and resolving customer complaints fairly, with mandatory reporting to the FCA and mechanisms to prevent recurring issues while maintaining customer relationships.
context: To establish complaint handling procedures that: Acknowledge all complaints promptly

name: Prompt Acknowledgement of All Complaints
description: A mandatory requirement that all complaints received by the bank must be acknowledged promptly to customers, establishing the initial procedural step in complaint handling.

name: Thorough Investigation of Complaint Issues
description: A mandatory requirement to conduct thorough investigations into the substance and circumstances of each complaint received.

name: Fair Resolution of Complaints
description: A mandatory requirement to resolve all complaints in a fair manner, ensuring equitable treatment and appropriate remediation.

name: FCA Reporting of Complaints
description: A mandatory reporting obligation requiring the bank to report complaints to the Financial Conduct Authority as required by regulatory rules.

name: Prevention of Repeat Complaint Issues
description: A mandatory requirement to implement measures and controls that prevent the recurrence of issues that have generated customer complaints.

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The primary financial services regulator in the United Kingdom to which complaint reports must be submitted in accordance with regulatory requirements.

name: Customer Complaint
description: A formal expression of dissatisfaction by a customer regarding the bank's products, services, or conduct, representing a compliance and reputational risk that must be managed through structured procedures.

name: Complaint Handler
description: The role responsible for receiving, acknowledging, investigating, and resolving customer complaints in accordance with the complaint handling policy and FCA requirements.

name: Customer
description: A natural person who holds a banking relationship with the bank and may submit a complaint regarding products, services, or conduct, triggering the complaint handling procedures.

name: Customer Complaints Policy
description: A policy governing the handling and resolution of customer complaints across all banking channels and products. The policy applies to all staff and covers complaints related to products, services, and policies.
context: Applies to: All customer complaints (product, service, policy)

name: Complaints Handling Obligation for All Staff
description: A mandatory requirement that all staff must handle customer complaints in accordance with this policy across all channels and for all account types and products.

name: All Staff
description: All bank staff members are responsible for handling customer complaints in accordance with the policy across all channels and for all products and accounts.

name: Account
description: All customer accounts are subject to the complaints policy, regardless of account type or product.

name: Banking Product
description: All banking products offered by the bank are subject to the customer complaints policy, including product-related complaints.

name: Customer
description: All customers who lodge complaints about products, services, or policies are covered by this complaints policy across all banking channels.

name: Service Complaint
description: Service-related complaints represent a compliance and operational risk that the policy is designed to address and manage.

name: Product Complaint
description: Product-related complaints represent a compliance and operational risk that the policy is designed to address and manage.

name: Policy Complaint
description: Policy-related complaints represent a compliance and operational risk that the policy is designed to address and manage.

name: Customer Complaints Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's formal policy governing the fair and timely resolution of customer complaints in accordance with regulatory requirements. The policy establishes the bank's commitment to treating all complaints seriously and resolving them within mandated regulatory timeframes.
context: FirstUK Bank treats all customer complaints seriously and resolves them fairly within regulatory timeframes.

name: Fair and Timely Complaint Resolution
description: Mandatory requirement that FirstUK Bank must resolve all customer complaints fairly and within regulatory timeframes. This provision establishes the operational standard for complaint handling across the bank.
context: FirstUK Bank treats all customer complaints seriously and resolves them fairly within regulatory timeframes.

name: All Staff
description: All FirstUK Bank staff members are collectively responsible for treating customer complaints seriously as part of the bank's commitment to fair complaint resolution and regulatory compliance.
context: FirstUK Bank treats all customer complaints seriously and resolves them fairly within regulatory timeframes.

name: Complaint Handling Risk
description: The risk of failing to resolve customer complaints fairly and within regulatory timeframes, which could result in regulatory breach, reputational damage, and customer dissatisfaction.
context: FirstUK Bank treats all customer complaints seriously and resolves them fairly within regulatory timeframes.

name: Complaints Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's policy governing the handling and resolution of customer complaints regarding service or product dissatisfaction. The policy establishes the foundational definition and scope of what constitutes a complaint within the bank's complaint management framework.
context: Any expression of dissatisfaction by customer about FirstUK Bank's service or product

name: Customer Dissatisfaction
description: The risk category encompassing customer expressions of dissatisfaction with FirstUK Bank's services or products, which triggers complaint handling obligations and potential regulatory reporting requirements.
context: Any expression of dissatisfaction by customer about FirstUK Bank's service or product

name: Customer
description: A natural person who holds or uses FirstUK Bank's services or products and may express dissatisfaction triggering the complaint definition and handling process.
context: Any expression of dissatisfaction by customer about FirstUK Bank's service or product

name: Long Processing Time
description: A service complaint category identifying delays in processing customer requests or transactions as a source of customer dissatisfaction and potential compliance concern.

name: Incorrect Information Provided
description: A service complaint category identifying the provision of inaccurate information to customers as a compliance and reputational risk.

name: Poor Customer Service
description: A service complaint category identifying substandard customer service delivery as a source of customer dissatisfaction and reputational harm.

name: System Error or Outage Impact
description: A service complaint category identifying system failures and service outages as operational risks affecting customer access and transaction processing.

name: Wrong Interest Rate Applied
description: A product complaint category identifying the incorrect application of contractual interest rates to customer accounts as a compliance and financial loss risk.

name: Fee Incorrectly Charged
description: A product complaint category identifying erroneous fee charges to customer accounts as a compliance and customer detriment risk.

name: Terms and Conditions Misunderstood
description: A product complaint category identifying customer confusion or misinterpretation of product terms and conditions as a source of disputes and compliance concern.

name: Feature Not Working
description: A product complaint category identifying non-functional product features as an operational risk affecting customer experience and product utility.

name: Unauthorized Transaction
description: A financial loss complaint category identifying transactions executed without customer authorization as a fraud and financial crime risk.

name: Fraudulent Activity
description: A financial loss complaint category identifying fraudulent conduct affecting customer accounts as a financial crime and customer detriment risk.

name: Incorrect Balance
description: A financial loss complaint category identifying inaccurate account balance reporting as an operational and compliance risk.

name: Fees Wrongly Charged
description: A financial loss complaint category identifying erroneous or unauthorized fee charges resulting in customer financial detriment.

name: Complaints Policy
description: Policy governing the receipt, logging, and handling of customer complaints across multiple channels including branch, phone, email, online portal, and letter. Establishes immediate logging requirements and designated contact points for complaint submission.
context: Letter (Complaints, FirstUK Bank, 125 Threadneedle Street, London)

name: Immediate Complaint Logging at Branch
description: Requirement that complaints received in person at a branch location must be logged immediately upon receipt.

name: Complaint Recording and Logging via Phone
description: Requirement that complaints received by phone must be recorded and logged. Establishes the designated phone channel for complaint submission.

name: Immediate Complaint Logging via Email
description: Requirement that complaints received via email must be logged immediately upon receipt at the designated email address.

name: Complaint Submission via Online Portal
description: Provision enabling customers to submit complaints through the online customer portal complaint form as an alternative channel.

name: Complaint Submission by Letter
description: Provision enabling customers to submit complaints by post to the designated FirstUK Bank complaints address.
context: Letter (Complaints, FirstUK Bank, 125 Threadneedle Street, London)

name: Phone Recording System
description: Technical control requiring recording of all phone-based complaint submissions to create an audit trail and ensure accurate logging of complaint details.

name: Online Customer Portal Complaint Form
description: Digital system enabling customers to submit complaints through a structured online form, creating an immediate electronic record of the complaint.

name: Branch Staff
description: Staff responsible for receiving complaints in person at branch locations and ensuring immediate logging of such complaints.

name: Phone Support Team
description: Staff responsible for receiving complaints via the designated phone channel, recording the call, and logging complaint details.

name: Email Support Team
description: Staff responsible for receiving complaints via email at the designated support address and ensuring immediate logging.

name: Customer
description: Individual customer with the right to submit complaints through multiple designated channels including branch, phone, email, online portal, or letter.

name: Complaints Handling Policy
description: Policy governing the immediate recording, acknowledgment, and logging of customer complaints across multiple channels (branch, phone, email, letter). Establishes timelines for acknowledgment and system documentation requirements.
context: Record Complaint - Date and time received, Customer name and account number, Complaint details (verbatim if verbal), Channel received through, Staff member receiving
Acknowledge to Customer - Branch: Immediate verbal acknowledgment + written confirmation
Log in System - Create complaint record in CRM, Assign complaint ID, Tag by category, Assign to appropriate handler

name: Mandatory Complaint Recording at Receipt
description: Requires staff to record the date, time, customer name, account number, complaint details verbatim (if verbal), channel of receipt, and receiving staff member upon complaint intake.
context: Record Complaint - Date and time received, Customer name and account number, Complaint details (verbatim if verbal), Channel received through, Staff member receiving

name: Immediate Verbal Acknowledgment for Branch Complaints
description: Mandates that complaints received in branch must receive immediate verbal acknowledgment followed by written confirmation to the customer.
context: Branch: Immediate verbal acknowledgment + written confirmation

name: Telephone Complaint Acknowledgment Within 24 Hours
description: Requires verbal acknowledgment of telephone complaints followed by written confirmation to be sent within 24 hours of receipt.
context: Phone: Verbal acknowledgment + written confirmation within 24 hours

name: Automated Receipt Confirmation for Email Complaints
description: Requires automated receipt confirmation to be sent to customers who submit complaints via email.

name: Written Acknowledgment for Letter Complaints Within 2 Business Days
description: Mandates written acknowledgment of complaints received by letter to be sent within 2 business days of receipt.
context: Letter: Written acknowledgment within 2 business days

name: Complaint System Logging and Assignment
description: Requires creation of complaint record in CRM system, assignment of unique complaint ID, categorization by complaint type, and assignment to appropriate handler.
context: Log in System - Create complaint record in CRM, Assign complaint ID, Tag by category, Assign to appropriate handler

name: Complaint Record Management System
description: CRM system used to create, track, and manage complaint records with unique identifiers, category tags, and handler assignment.

name: Complaint Handler
description: Staff member assigned responsibility for managing and processing individual customer complaints after initial recording and acknowledgment.

name: Staff Member Receiving Complaint
description: Any staff member who receives a customer complaint is responsible for recording the complaint details and initiating the acknowledgment process according to the channel used.

name: Complaint Customer
description: Customer who submits a complaint through any channel (branch, phone, email, or letter) and is entitled to acknowledgment and system logging of their complaint.

name: Complaint Handling Policy
description: A policy governing the initial assessment and triage of customer complaints based on severity criteria. The policy establishes a two-tier classification system distinguishing urgent complaints requiring immediate escalation from standard complaints processed through normal channels.

name: Urgent Complaint Escalation to Manager
description: A mandatory requirement to escalate complaints meeting urgent criteria to a manager immediately. Urgent complaints are defined as those involving financial loss exceeding £1,000, fraud or security breaches, service outages, or regulatory concerns.
context: Urgent (Immediate Action): → Escalate to Manager immediately

name: Standard Complaint Processing
description: A mandatory requirement to process standard complaints through normal channels. Standard complaints include regular service issues, fee disputes under £1,000, and operational delays.

name: Initial Assessment Completion Timeframe
description: A requirement that the initial assessment and triage of complaints be completed within one to two days of receipt.

name: Financial Loss Risk
description: A risk category identifying complaints involving customer financial loss exceeding £1,000 as requiring urgent escalation and immediate management attention.

name: Fraud and Security Breach Risk
description: A risk category identifying complaints involving fraud or security breaches as requiring urgent escalation and immediate management attention.

name: Service Outage Impact Risk
description: A risk category identifying complaints involving service outages as requiring urgent escalation and immediate management attention.

name: Regulatory Concern Risk
description: A risk category identifying complaints involving regulatory concerns as requiring urgent escalation and immediate management attention.

name: Manager
description: A role responsible for receiving and handling urgent complaint escalations immediately upon notification by the triage function.

name: Fraud Investigation Policy
description: Policy governing the investigation phase of fraud cases, spanning days 2–5 post-detection. Establishes mandatory procedures for information gathering, documentation, staff interviews, and determination of bank liability.

name: Account Records Review Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to review account records as part of fraud investigation. This is a discrete investigative step performed during the investigation phase.

name: Transaction History Review Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to check transaction history during fraud investigation to identify suspicious or unauthorized activity patterns.

name: Relevant Procedures and Policies Review Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to review relevant procedures and policies applicable to the fraud case during investigation to establish the regulatory and operational framework.

name: Staff Interview Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to interview involved staff members where applicable during fraud investigation to gather firsthand accounts and operational context.

name: Policy Compliance Assessment Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to assess whether the bank's policies and procedures were complied with during the incident under investigation.

name: Investigation Findings Documentation Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to record all findings discovered during the fraud investigation, creating a documented audit trail of the investigative process.

name: Applicable Policy and Procedure Documentation Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to document which policies and procedures are applicable to the fraud case being investigated.

name: Bank Liability Determination Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to determine whether FirstUK Bank bears responsibility or fault for the fraud incident during investigation.
context: Determine if FirstUK Bank at fault

name: Financial Loss Quantification Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to quantify any financial loss resulting from the fraud incident, where applicable, to establish the monetary impact.

name: Fraud
description: Fraud risk addressed by this investigation policy, encompassing unauthorized transactions, account takeover, and other fraudulent activities requiring investigation and resolution.
context: Determine if FirstUK Bank at fault

name: FirstUK Bank
description: The financial institution responsible for implementing fraud investigation procedures and determining its own liability in fraud cases.
context: Determine if FirstUK Bank at fault

name: Complaints Resolution Policy
description: Policy governing the resolution phase of customer complaints (Days 5–8), defining possible outcomes based on fault determination and the bank's obligations for compensation, interest, apologies, and process improvements.
context: Plus interest (8% per annum) if appropriate

name: Full Financial Compensation for Loss
description: Mandatory requirement that FirstUK Bank provide full financial compensation to the customer when the bank is found at fault in a complaint.

name: Interest Payment on Compensation
description: Requirement to pay interest at 8% per annum on compensation amounts when appropriate, as part of the bank's remediation obligation when at fault.
context: Plus interest (8% per annum) if appropriate

name: Additional Compensation for Distress
description: Provision requiring the bank to provide additional compensation beyond financial loss when the customer has suffered distress as a result of the bank's fault.
context: Plus additional compensation if distress caused

name: Written Apology Requirement
description: Requirement that FirstUK Bank issue a written apology to the customer when the bank is found at fault in a complaint.

name: Process Improvement Following Fault
description: Obligation to implement process improvements when the bank is at fault, designed to prevent recurrence of the issue that led to the complaint.

name: Policy and Procedure Explanation When Customer at Fault
description: When a complaint is resolved against the customer, the bank must provide an explanation of the relevant policy or procedure in an educational tone to help the customer understand.

name: Evidence Provision When Customer at Fault
description: Requirement to provide evidence to the customer supporting the bank's decision when the complaint is resolved against the customer.

name: Polite Decline of Compensation When Customer at Fault
description: Provision prohibiting compensation when the complaint investigation determines the customer is at fault, with the bank declining compensation in a polite manner.

name: Explanation of Evidence in Inconclusive Cases
description: When a complaint resolution is unclear or inconclusive, the bank must explain the evidence reviewed and acknowledge the customer's perspective.

name: Partial Compensation in Inconclusive Cases
description: Provision allowing the bank to offer partial compensation when a complaint resolution is inconclusive or unclear, if appropriate.

name: External Ombudsman Referral Explanation
description: Requirement to explain further steps available to the customer, including the option to escalate to an external ombudsman when a complaint resolution is inconclusive.

name: FirstUK Bank
description: The financial institution responsible for implementing the complaints resolution policy, determining fault, and providing appropriate remedies and responses to customers.

name: Customer
description: The party filing a complaint against FirstUK Bank, who may receive compensation, interest, apologies, or educational explanations depending on the resolution outcome.

name: Complaint Resolution Fault
description: The risk that FirstUK Bank may be found at fault in a customer complaint, triggering obligations for financial compensation, interest, apologies, and process improvements.
context: Plus interest (8% per annum) if appropriate

name: Written Response to Customer Complaint
description: A mandatory requirement that the bank must provide a written response to a customer complaint by Day 8, containing specific elements including acknowledgment, investigation summary, decision with reasoning, compensation details if applicable, and escalation rights. The response must be delivered via the customer's preferred channel (email or letter) in plain language with a professional and respectful tone.
context: Written Response Must Include: Acknowledgment of complaint, Summary of investigation, Clear decision and reasoning, Compensation offered (if applicable), Explanation of right to escalate
Delivery: Email or letter (customer choice), Plain language (avoid jargon), Tone: Professional, respectful

name: Complaint Acknowledgment Requirement
description: The bank must acknowledge receipt of the customer complaint as part of the written response on Day 8.

name: Investigation Summary Requirement
description: The bank must provide a summary of the investigation conducted into the customer complaint as part of the written response.

name: Clear Decision and Reasoning Requirement
description: The bank must provide a clear decision on the complaint with detailed reasoning explaining the basis for that decision in the written response.

name: Compensation Disclosure Requirement
description: Where applicable, the bank must clearly state any compensation offered to the customer in the written response.

name: Escalation Rights Explanation Requirement
description: The bank must explain the customer's right to escalate the complaint to a higher authority or external body in the written response.

name: Plain Language Communication Requirement
description: The written response must be delivered in plain language that avoids jargon and is easily understood by the customer.

name: Customer Choice of Delivery Channel
description: The bank must allow the customer to choose their preferred delivery method for the written response, either email or letter.

name: Professional and Respectful Tone Requirement
description: The written response must be delivered with a professional and respectful tone toward the customer.

name: Response Timeframes Policy
description: Policy establishing maximum response times for customer complaints under FCA requirements, with differentiated timeframes based on complaint complexity and escalation procedures. Defines the 8-week clock mechanism and conditions for extension.
context: Stops: When response sent to customer
Can be extended 8 weeks if: Complex investigation justified, customer agrees

name: Financial Conduct Authority Complaints Requirements
description: FCA regulatory requirements governing complaint response timeframes, escalation procedures, and the 8-week resolution clock for financial services complaints.

name: Simple Complaint Resolution Within One Business Day
description: Requirement to resolve simple complaints that can be resolved quickly within 1 business day, with escalation to Manager if further action is needed.
context: Simple (resolve quickly) | 1 business day | Manager if escalated

name: Standard Complaint Resolution Within Eight Calendar Days
description: Requirement to resolve standard complaints within 8 calendar days, with escalation to Director if the complaint remains unresolved within this timeframe.
context: Standard | 8 calendar days | Director if unresolved

name: Complex Complaint Resolution Within Eight Weeks
description: Requirement to resolve complex complaints within 8 weeks under FCA extension provisions, with mandatory FCA notification if this timeframe is exceeded.
context: Complex | 8 weeks (FCA extension) | FCA notification if exceeded
Stops: When response sent to customer

name: Eight-Week Clock Extension for Complex Investigation
description: Provision allowing extension of the 8-week complaint resolution clock for an additional 8 weeks when complex investigation is justified and the customer agrees to the extension.
context: Can be extended 8 weeks if: Complex investigation justified, customer agrees

name: Manager
description: Role responsible for escalation and handling of simple complaints that cannot be resolved within 1 business day.

name: Director
description: Role responsible for escalation and handling of standard complaints that remain unresolved after 8 calendar days.

name: Complaint Resolution Delay
description: Risk of failing to meet FCA-mandated complaint response timeframes, resulting in regulatory breach and potential FCA notification requirements.
context: Can be extended 8 weeks if: Complex investigation justified

name: Complaint Handling Policy
description: Policy governing the handling, investigation, and resolution of customer service complaints. Establishes procedures for timeline review, staff interviews, and compensation determination based on fault and impact severity.
context: Investigation: Check timeline, Review procedures followed, Assess reasonableness, Interview staff if needed
Resolution: If at fault: Apology + compensation for inconvenience

name: Service Complaint Investigation Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to investigate service complaints through a structured process including timeline verification, procedure review, reasonableness assessment, and staff interviews where necessary.

name: Fault-Based Compensation Obligation
description: Obligation to provide apology and compensation when the bank is found at fault, with compensation levels scaled to the severity of inconvenience or distress caused to the customer.
context: If at fault: Apology + compensation for inconvenience
Compensation: Up to £100 for minor inconvenience, more if significant distress/loss

name: Process Improvement Following Complaint Resolution
description: Requirement to implement process improvements and preventive measures following complaint resolution to prevent recurrence of identified service failures.
context: Learning: Process improvement to prevent recurrence

name: Service Failure Risk
description: Operational risk category encompassing service delivery failures such as long wait times, provision of incorrect information, and poor staff conduct that may result in customer complaints and reputational damage.
context: Example: Long wait, incorrect information, rude staff

name: Complaint Investigation Officer
description: Role responsible for conducting structured investigations into service complaints, including timeline verification, procedure review, reasonableness assessment, and staff interviews.

name: Complaint Resolution Authority
description: Role responsible for determining fault, authorizing compensation, and ensuring process improvements are implemented following complaint resolution.
context: If at fault: Apology + compensation for inconvenience
Compensation: Up to £100 for minor inconvenience, more if significant distress/loss
Learning: Process improvement to prevent recurrence

name: Complaint Timeline Review
description: Control measure requiring verification and review of complaint timelines to establish the sequence of events and identify service failure points.

name: Procedure Compliance Audit
description: Control measure requiring review of procedures followed during the service interaction to determine whether established protocols were correctly executed.

name: Staff Interview Process
description: Control measure enabling investigation teams to conduct interviews with staff members involved in the complaint incident to gather firsthand accounts and clarify procedural adherence.

name: Fee Disputes Policy
description: Policy governing the investigation and resolution of customer complaints regarding unexpected charges, overdraft fees, and card replacement fees. Establishes investigation procedures including review of terms and conditions, fee application accuracy, and disclosure clarity, with resolution pathways based on investigation findings.
context: Unexpected charge, overdraft fee, card replacement fee
If fee applied correctly per T&Cs: Explain and decline reversal

name: Fee Dispute Investigation Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to investigate fee disputes by reviewing terms and conditions, verifying correct fee application, assessing clarity of fee disclosure, and reviewing customer account history.

name: Fee Dispute Resolution - Correct Application
description: When investigation confirms fee was applied correctly per terms and conditions, the bank must explain the fee to the customer and decline reversal.
context: If fee applied correctly per T&Cs: Explain and decline reversal

name: Fee Dispute Resolution - Error Correction
description: When investigation identifies a fee application error, the bank must reverse the charge and provide interest compensation to the customer.
context: If fee error: Reverse charge + interest

name: Fee Dispute Resolution - Unclear Terms
description: When investigation determines that terms and conditions were unclear regarding fee disclosure, the bank must refund the charge and provide an apology to the customer.

name: Unexpected Charge
description: Risk category covering customer complaints regarding charges that were not anticipated or clearly disclosed, requiring investigation and potential remediation.
context: Unexpected charge, overdraft fee, card replacement fee

name: Overdraft Fee
description: Risk category covering disputes related to overdraft fees charged to customer accounts, requiring investigation of application accuracy and disclosure clarity.
context: Unexpected charge, overdraft fee, card replacement fee

name: Card Replacement Fee
description: Risk category covering disputes related to fees charged for card replacement services, requiring investigation of correct application and disclosure.
context: Unexpected charge, overdraft fee, card replacement fee

name: Terms and Conditions Review
description: Control measure requiring review of applicable terms and conditions during fee dispute investigation to verify fee application accuracy and disclosure requirements.
context: Check if fee applied correctly per T&Cs

name: Customer History Review
description: Control measure requiring review of customer account history as part of fee dispute investigation to assess patterns and context of disputed charges.

name: Fee Disclosure Assessment
description: Control measure requiring assessment of whether fees were disclosed clearly to the customer, used to determine appropriate resolution pathway.

name: Account Balance Discrepancy
description: A risk category covering situations where customer account balances are incorrect, credits are missing, or interest calculations are wrong. This includes discrepancies arising from bank errors, customer misunderstanding, or system failures.
context: Missing credit, wrong balance shown, interest miscalculated
If bank error: Correct balance + interest on missing amount
If system error: Urgent IT escalation to fix

name: Transaction Reconciliation Requirement
description: A mandatory requirement to reconcile all transactions on an account when investigating balance discrepancies. This is part of the investigation process to identify the root cause of balance issues.
context: Investigation: Reconcile transactions, Check system records, Verify calculations

name: System Records Verification
description: A mandatory requirement to check and verify system records when investigating account balance issues. This ensures that recorded transactions match actual system data.
context: Investigation: Reconcile transactions, Check system records, Verify calculations

name: Calculation Verification
description: A mandatory requirement to verify all calculations, particularly interest calculations, when investigating account balance discrepancies.
context: Investigation: Reconcile transactions, Check system records, Verify calculations

name: Hold Period Review
description: A mandatory requirement to review any hold periods on funds when investigating account balance issues, as holds may explain apparent missing credits.
context: Investigation: Reconcile transactions, Check system records, Verify calculations, Review any hold periods

name: Bank Error Balance Correction
description: An obligation to correct the account balance and pay interest on any missing amount when the investigation determines that a bank error caused the discrepancy.
context: If bank error: Correct balance + interest on missing amount

name: Customer Education on Balance Issues
description: An obligation to educate and explain balance discrepancies to customers when the issue results from customer misunderstanding, without imposing penalties.
context: If customer misunderstanding: Explain (educate, don't penalize)

name: System Error IT Escalation
description: An obligation to escalate system errors urgently to the IT department for immediate remediation when a system error is identified as the cause of a balance discrepancy.
context: If system error: Urgent IT escalation to fix

name: Transaction Reconciliation Process
description: A control measure requiring reconciliation of transactions to identify discrepancies and verify account accuracy during balance issue investigations.
context: Investigation: Reconcile transactions, Check system records, Verify calculations

name: System Records Audit
description: A control measure requiring verification of system records to ensure that recorded transactions and balances are accurate and complete.
context: Investigation: Reconcile transactions, Check system records, Verify calculations

name: Calculation Verification Control
description: A control measure requiring verification of all calculations, particularly interest calculations, to ensure mathematical accuracy in account balances.
context: Investigation: Reconcile transactions, Check system records, Verify calculations

name: Unauthorized Transaction
description: A financial transaction on a customer account that the customer claims was not authorized by them. The policy requires investigation to determine whether fraud occurred, customer liability applies, or the transaction remains disputed.

name: Fraudulent Transaction Investigation
description: The investigation process triggered when a customer reports a potentially fraudulent transaction. The investigation includes obtaining statements, reviewing transaction details, checking authorization status, and assessing fraud likelihood, with escalation to the fraud team if needed.

name: Fraudulent Transaction Reimbursement Within 10 Business Days
description: When fraud is confirmed on a customer account, the bank must provide full reimbursement to the customer within 10 business days and issue an apology.
context: If fraud confirmed: Full reimbursement within 10 business days + apology

name: Customer Liability Explanation for Unauthorized Transactions
description: When investigation determines the customer is liable for an unauthorized transaction, the bank must provide an explanation to the customer in an educational manner.

name: Disputed Transaction Further Investigation and FCA Guidance
description: When a transaction remains disputed after initial investigation, the bank must conduct further investigation and apply FCA guidance in determining resolution.
context: If disputed: Further investigation + FCA guidance

name: Fraud Policy
description: The bank's formal policy governing fraud detection, investigation, and resolution procedures for unauthorized transactions and customer fraud claims.

name: Customer
description: A natural person who holds a bank account and may report fraudulent or unauthorized transactions for investigation and resolution.

name: Fraud Team
description: The operational team responsible for investigating fraud alerts and unauthorized transaction claims when escalation from initial review is required.

name: Disputed Transaction
description: A financial transaction on a customer account that remains unresolved after investigation, requiring further inquiry and application of FCA guidance.
context: If disputed: Further investigation + FCA guidance

name: Account Takeover
description: A fraud scenario where a customer's account is used without authorization, typically involving compromise of authentication credentials or identity theft. The policy defines investigation and resolution procedures including immediate account freeze, transaction review, and customer reimbursement.
context: Customer discovers account used without permission

name: Account Takeover Investigation
description: The investigation process triggered when a customer reports unauthorized account access. The procedure includes immediate account freeze, transaction review, authentication review, fraud team escalation, and potential law enforcement notification.

name: Immediate Account Freeze
description: An emergency protective measure executed immediately upon discovery of unauthorized account access to prevent further fraudulent transactions and protect customer assets.

name: Transaction Review
description: A review of account transactions to identify and document fraudulent activity following an account takeover incident.
context: Investigation: Immediate account freeze, Transaction review

name: Authentication Review
description: An examination of customer authentication mechanisms, including password changes and access credentials, to determine how unauthorized access was gained and to prevent recurrence.

name: Fraud Team
description: The team responsible for escalation and investigation of account takeover incidents, including coordination of investigation activities and law enforcement notification.

name: Law Enforcement Notification
description: The process of notifying law enforcement authorities when an account takeover incident warrants criminal investigation, performed as part of the fraud investigation procedure.

name: Fraudulent Transaction Reimbursement
description: The bank's obligation to provide full reimbursement to customers for transactions executed without authorization as part of account takeover resolution.
context: Resolution: Full reimbursement of fraudulent transactions

name: Account Security Reset
description: A remedial control measure that resets account security settings following an account takeover incident to restore customer protection.

name: Replacement Card
description: A new payment card issued to the customer as part of account takeover resolution to replace potentially compromised card details.

name: Online Access Reset
description: A reset of online banking access credentials and settings performed as part of account takeover resolution to prevent further unauthorized access.

name: Credit Monitoring
description: A protective service offered to customers when account takeover involves identity theft, providing ongoing monitoring of credit activity to detect further fraudulent use of personal information.

name: Regular Follow-up
description: Ongoing contact and support provided to customers following account takeover resolution to ensure their concerns are addressed and no further unauthorized activity occurs.

name: Customer
description: The individual customer who discovers and reports unauthorized account access, and who is the subject of investigation and resolution procedures including reimbursement and account security restoration.
context: Customer discovers account used without permission

name: Complaint Escalation Policy
description: A policy governing the escalation of customer complaints through defined authority levels based on severity, financial loss, and involvement triggers. The policy establishes timelines and decision-makers at each escalation stage, from frontline resolution through CEO/Board review.
context: Escalation Triggers: Complaint unresolved after manager review, Financial compensation >£500 (Director) or >£2,000 (CEO), Regulatory or reputational concern

name: Frontline Complaint Resolution Requirement
description: Customer Service Agents must resolve simple, low-value complaints at frontline level within one day.
context: Frontline | Customer Service Agent | <1 day | Simple, low-value

name: Manager-Level Complaint Review Requirement
description: Complaints Managers must review and resolve moderate issues involving losses under £500 within five days.
context: Manager | Complaints Manager | <5 days | Moderate issues, <£500 loss

name: Director-Level Complaint Review Requirement
description: Head of Customer Service must review significant complaints involving losses between £500 and £2,000 within eight days.
context: Director | Head of Customer Service | <8 days | Significant issues, £500–£2,000 loss

name: CEO/Board Escalation Requirement
description: Major complaints involving losses exceeding £2,000, major failures, or reputational risk must be escalated to CEO/Board for review within eight weeks or longer.
context: Escalated | CEO/Board | 8+ weeks | Major failures, >£2,000 loss, reputational risk

name: Escalation Trigger - Unresolved After Manager Review
description: Any complaint that remains unresolved following manager review must be escalated to the next authority level.
context: Escalation Triggers: Complaint unresolved after manager review

name: Escalation Trigger - Financial Compensation Threshold
description: Complaints requiring financial compensation exceeding £500 must be escalated to Director level; those exceeding £2,000 must reach CEO/Board.

name: Escalation Trigger - Regulatory or Reputational Concern
description: Complaints involving regulatory or reputational concerns must be escalated beyond manager level.

name: Escalation Trigger - Media or Legal Involvement
description: Complaints involving media or legal involvement must be escalated to senior management or CEO/Board.

name: Escalation Trigger - FCA Customer Escalation
description: Any complaint escalated by the customer to the FCA must trigger immediate escalation within the bank's hierarchy.

name: Customer Service Agent
description: Customer Service Agents are responsible for resolving simple, low-value complaints at the frontline within one day.
context: Frontline | Customer Service Agent | <1 day | Simple, low-value

name: Complaints Manager
description: Complaints Managers are responsible for reviewing and resolving moderate complaints involving losses under £500 within five days.
context: Manager | Complaints Manager | <5 days | Moderate issues, <£500 loss

name: Head of Customer Service
description: Head of Customer Service is responsible for reviewing significant complaints involving losses between £500 and £2,000 within eight days.
context: Director | Head of Customer Service | <8 days | Significant issues, £500–£2,000 loss

name: CEO/Board
description: CEO and Board are responsible for reviewing and deciding on major complaints involving losses exceeding £2,000, major failures, or significant reputational risk within eight weeks or longer.
context: Escalated | CEO/Board | 8+ weeks | Major failures, >£2,000 loss, reputational risk

name: Reputational Risk
description: Reputational risk is identified as a trigger for escalation to CEO/Board level, particularly when complaints involve media or legal involvement or result in significant financial loss.

name: Regulatory Compliance Risk
description: Regulatory compliance risk is identified as an escalation trigger when complaints involve regulatory concerns or FCA involvement.

name: Compensation Framework
description: A policy establishing financial compensation guidelines for customers affected by service delays, service failures, financial errors, and serious distress. The framework defines compensation ranges based on severity and duration of impact, with approval thresholds tied to compensation amount.
context: Financial loss (error) | Full loss + 8% interest | Actual loss + interest

name: Service Delay Compensation for One to Two Days
description: Requires compensation of £0–£50 for service delays lasting 1–2 days, based on inconvenience caused to the customer.

name: Service Delay Compensation for Three to Five Days
description: Requires compensation of £50–£100 for service delays lasting 3–5 days, reflecting operational disruption to the customer.

name: Service Failure Compensation for More Than Five Days
description: Requires compensation of £100–£300 for service failures exceeding 5 days, reflecting significant impact on the customer.

name: Financial Loss Compensation with Interest
description: Requires compensation equal to the full financial loss incurred by the customer plus 8% interest, covering errors that result in actual monetary loss.
context: Financial loss (error) | Full loss + 8% interest | Actual loss + interest

name: Serious Distress Compensation
description: Requires compensation of £250–£500 or more for cases involving serious distress, recognizing emotional impact on the customer.

name: Complaints Manager Approval for Compensation Under £500
description: Requires Complaints Manager approval for compensation awards below £500.

name: Director Approval for Compensation Between £500 and £2,000
description: Requires Director approval for compensation awards between £500 and £2,000.

name: CEO Approval for Compensation Over £2,000
description: Requires CEO approval for compensation awards exceeding £2,000.

name: Board Notification and CEO Approval for Compensation Over £5,000
description: Requires both Board notification and CEO approval for compensation awards exceeding £5,000.

name: Complaints Manager
description: Role responsible for approving compensation awards below £500 under the Compensation Framework.

name: Director
description: Role responsible for approving compensation awards between £500 and £2,000 under the Compensation Framework.

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: Role responsible for approving compensation awards exceeding £2,000 and for Board notification of awards exceeding £5,000 under the Compensation Framework.

name: Board
description: Role responsible for receiving notification of compensation awards exceeding £5,000 under the Compensation Framework.

name: Service Delay
description: Operational risk arising from delays in service delivery lasting 1–5 days, resulting in inconvenience or operational disruption to customers.

name: Service Failure
description: Operational risk arising from service failures exceeding 5 days, resulting in significant impact to customers.

name: Financial Error
description: Operational risk arising from errors that result in actual financial loss to customers, requiring full compensation plus interest.
context: Financial loss (error) | Full loss + 8% interest | Actual loss + interest

name: Customer Distress
description: Reputational and operational risk arising from serious distress caused to customers by service failures or errors.

name: FCA Reporting Policy
description: Policy governing the identification and reporting of complaints to the Financial Conduct Authority. Establishes mandatory reporting obligations for complaints alleging breaches of FCA rules, complaints about financial services and conduct, complaints causing financial loss, and systemic issues.
context: Complaints alleging breaches of FCA rules

name: Mandatory Reporting of FCA Rule Breaches
description: Requirement to report to the FCA any complaint that alleges a breach of FCA rules. This is a discrete mandatory reporting obligation under the FCA Reporting Policy.
context: Complaints alleging breaches of FCA rules

name: Mandatory Reporting of Financial Services Complaints
description: Requirement to report to the FCA any complaint concerning financial services. This provision ensures complaints about the delivery or quality of financial services are escalated to the regulator.

name: Mandatory Reporting of Conduct Complaints
description: Requirement to report to the FCA any complaint relating to conduct. This provision captures complaints about staff or organisational behaviour that may breach regulatory standards.

name: Mandatory Reporting of Complaints Causing Financial Loss
description: Requirement to report to the FCA any complaint that results in or alleges financial loss to the customer. This provision ensures material harm events are escalated to the regulator.

name: Mandatory Reporting of Systemic Issues
description: Requirement to report to the FCA complaints that indicate systemic issues within the organisation. This provision captures patterns or widespread problems that may affect multiple customers or represent structural compliance failures.

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The UK financial regulator to which complaints meeting specified criteria must be reported. The FCA is the primary recipient of escalated complaints under this policy.
context: Complaints alleging breaches of FCA rules

name: Conduct Risk
description: Risk arising from complaints about staff or organisational conduct that may breach FCA rules or regulatory standards. This risk category is addressed through mandatory reporting of conduct-related complaints.

name: Financial Loss Risk
description: Risk of customer financial harm resulting from service failures or breaches. Complaints causing financial loss are flagged for FCA reporting to ensure material harm events are escalated.

name: Systemic Compliance Risk
description: Risk arising from patterns or widespread issues within the organisation that affect multiple customers or indicate structural compliance failures. Systemic issues must be reported to the FCA.

name: FCA Reporting Requirement
description: Policy governing FirstUK Bank's obligation to file aggregated complaint statistics to the FCA on a quarterly basis. The policy establishes the reporting cadence, data scope, and disclosure framework for complaints handling under COBS rules.
context: As data to FCA, not automatically disclosed

name: Quarterly Aggregated Complaint Statistics Filing
description: Mandatory requirement for FirstUK Bank to submit aggregated complaint statistics to the FCA on a quarterly basis. This is a discrete reporting obligation distinct from individual complaint handling.
context: As data to FCA, not automatically disclosed

name: Customer Escalation Right to FCA After Eight Weeks
description: Provision allowing customers to escalate unresolved complaints to the FCA after eight weeks of non-resolution by FirstUK Bank. This establishes the customer's right to external regulatory escalation.
context: Customers can escalate to FCA if unresolved after 8 weeks

name: Conduct of Business Sourcebook
description: FCA regulatory rulebook governing conduct of business requirements, including complaints handling and reporting obligations. COBS establishes the framework under which FirstUK Bank must report complaint statistics and manage customer escalations.

name: Complaints Handling Risk
description: The risk that FirstUK Bank fails to properly handle, track, or report customer complaints in accordance with FCA COBS requirements, resulting in regulatory breach or customer detriment.
context: Customers can escalate to FCA if unresolved after 8 weeks

name: FirstUK Bank
description: The regulated entity responsible for filing aggregated complaint statistics to the FCA on a quarterly basis and managing the complaints escalation process in accordance with COBS.
context: Who Files: FirstUK Bank (directly to FCA)

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The UK financial regulator that receives quarterly aggregated complaint statistics from FirstUK Bank and provides the escalation pathway for unresolved customer complaints.
context: As data to FCA, not automatically disclosed
Customers can escalate to FCA if unresolved after 8 weeks

name: FCA Escalation and Complaints Handling Policy
description: Policy governing the escalation of customer complaints to the Financial Conduct Authority and Financial Ombudsman Service when customers are dissatisfied with FirstUK Bank's response. Establishes the bank's obligation to provide FCA contact information, FOS details, and binding escalation procedures.
context: If Customer Unhappy: FirstUK Bank provides FCA contact information
Customer can escalate to Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS)
FOS is independent, free to customer

name: Provision of FCA Contact Information to Dissatisfied Customers
description: FirstUK Bank must provide customers with FCA contact information when they express dissatisfaction with the bank's complaint response.
context: If Customer Unhappy: FirstUK Bank provides FCA contact information

name: Customer Right to Escalate to Financial Ombudsman Service
description: Customers have the right to escalate complaints to the Financial Ombudsman Service, which is independent and free to the customer, with binding decision authority.
context: Customer can escalate to Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS)
FOS is independent, free to customer

name: Escalation Letter Content Requirements
description: Escalation letters must include a statement of customer rights, FOS contact details, and notification of the 6-month escalation time limit from the bank's final response.
context: Escalation Letter Must Include: Statement of rights
Time limit: Customer must escalate within 6 months of final response

name: Six-Month Escalation Deadline to Financial Ombudsman Service
description: Customers must escalate their complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service within 6 months of receiving the bank's final response.
context: Time limit: Customer must escalate within 6 months of final response

name: Financial Ombudsman Service
description: Independent external authority responsible for adjudicating customer complaints escalated by FirstUK Bank customers. FOS decisions are binding on the bank.
context: Customer can escalate to Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS)
FOS is independent, free to customer

name: FirstUK Bank Complaints Escalation Responsibility
description: FirstUK Bank is responsible for providing FCA contact information to dissatisfied customers and ensuring escalation letters contain all required information including FOS contact details and time limits.
context: FirstUK Bank provides FCA contact information
Escalation Letter Must Include: Statement of rights, FOS contact: 0800 023 4567, www.financialombudsman.org.uk

name: Dissatisfied Customer
description: A FirstUK Bank customer who is unhappy with the bank's complaint response and has the right to escalate to the Financial Ombudsman Service.
context: If Customer Unhappy: FirstUK Bank provides FCA contact information
Customer can escalate to Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS)

name: Complaints Policy
description: A policy governing the tracking, recording, and management of customer complaints. The policy mandates capture of complaint metadata including date, type, category, customer details, resolution outcome, compensation, and resolution timeframe to ensure systematic complaint handling and regulatory compliance.

name: Complaint Date Recording
description: A mandatory requirement to record and track the date on which each complaint is received. This provision ensures temporal accountability and enables monitoring of complaint resolution timelines.

name: Complaint Type and Category Classification
description: A mandatory requirement to classify and record the type and category of each complaint received. This provision enables systematic categorisation and trend analysis of complaint patterns.

name: Customer Details Recording
description: A mandatory requirement to capture and retain customer details associated with each complaint. This provision ensures proper identification and linkage of complaints to customer accounts.

name: Complaint Outcome Documentation
description: A mandatory requirement to record the outcome of each complaint investigation, categorised as upheld, rejected, or partial. This provision ensures transparent documentation of complaint resolution decisions.

name: Compensation Payment Recording
description: A mandatory requirement to record and track compensation paid to customers as a result of complaint resolution. This provision ensures financial accountability and audit trail for complaint-related payments.

name: Time to Resolution Tracking
description: A mandatory requirement to measure and record the time taken to resolve each complaint from receipt to final outcome. This provision enables monitoring of complaint handling efficiency and regulatory compliance with resolution timeframes.

name: Complaint Handling Risk
description: The risk that complaints are not properly tracked, categorised, or resolved in accordance with regulatory requirements. This includes risks of inadequate record-keeping, delayed resolution, and failure to identify systemic issues through complaint trend analysis.

name: Complaints Handling and Reporting Policy
description: A policy governing the reporting and analytics of customer complaints to internal management, the Board, and the Financial Conduct Authority. The policy establishes mandatory reporting cadences and content requirements at monthly, quarterly, and annual intervals, with specific metrics and trend analysis obligations.

name: Monthly Complaints Report to Management
description: Mandatory monthly reporting obligation requiring submission of complaints data to management, including total complaints received, average resolution time, upheld versus rejected ratio, financial compensation paid, and identified trends and patterns.

name: Quarterly Complaints Report to Board
description: Mandatory quarterly reporting obligation requiring submission of complaints analysis to the Board, including complaint volume trends, top complaint types, systemic issues identified, and corrective actions taken.

name: Annual Complaints Report to FCA
description: Mandatory annual reporting obligation to the Financial Conduct Authority requiring submission of aggregate complaints statistics, complaint handling effectiveness metrics, and documentation of process improvements implemented.

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The UK financial regulator to which the bank must submit annual aggregate complaints statistics and complaint handling effectiveness reports as mandated by this policy.

name: Board
description: The Board receives quarterly reports on complaint volume trends, top complaint types, systemic issues, and corrective actions taken, establishing accountability for complaints management at the governance level.

name: Management
description: Management receives monthly complaints reports detailing total complaints, resolution times, upheld versus rejected ratios, compensation paid, and identified trends and patterns for operational oversight.

name: Complaints Learning and Improvement Policy
description: A policy framework requiring the bank to identify systemic complaint patterns, analyze root causes, implement corrective actions, and monitor their effectiveness. The policy mandates a structured approach to complaints management that goes beyond individual resolution to drive organizational improvement.
context: Identify systemic complaints (same issue, multiple customers)

name: Systemic Complaint Identification Requirement
description: Banks must identify complaints that represent systemic issues — the same problem affecting multiple customers — rather than treating each complaint in isolation. This provision requires pattern recognition across the complaint population.
context: Identify systemic complaints (same issue, multiple customers)

name: Root Cause Analysis Obligation
description: Once systemic complaints are identified, the bank must conduct a root cause analysis to understand the underlying reason for the complaint pattern, not merely the surface symptom.

name: Corrective Action Implementation Requirement
description: The bank must implement corrective actions in response to identified root causes. This provision mandates that analysis must be followed by concrete remedial steps to address systemic issues.

name: Corrective Action Effectiveness Monitoring
description: The bank must monitor the effectiveness of corrective actions implemented in response to systemic complaints. This provision requires ongoing evaluation to ensure that remedial measures actually resolve the underlying issue.

name: Slow Processing
description: A complaint category identified in the policy as an example of a systemic issue that may arise from inadequate Standard Operating Procedures or insufficient resource allocation. The policy illustrates that slow processing complaints should trigger SOP review and resource augmentation.
context: High 'slow processing' complaints → Review SOP, add resources

name: Fee Dispute
description: A complaint category identified as a systemic issue that may result from unclear Terms and Conditions or inadequate fee disclosure. The policy indicates that multiple fee disputes should trigger improved T&C clarity and better customer disclosure.
context: Multiple fee disputes → Improve T&C clarity, better disclosure

name: Fraud
description: A complaint category identified as a systemic issue that may indicate weaknesses in security measures. The policy illustrates that fraud complaints should trigger strengthened security controls.

name: Standard Operating Procedure Review
description: A control measure requiring review of Standard Operating Procedures when systemic complaints (such as slow processing) are identified. This measure ensures that operational processes are evaluated and improved in response to complaint patterns.
context: High 'slow processing' complaints → Review SOP, add resources

name: Resource Allocation Adjustment
description: A control measure requiring the bank to add resources when systemic complaints indicate resource constraints. This measure addresses operational bottlenecks identified through complaint analysis.
context: High 'slow processing' complaints → Review SOP, add resources

name: Terms and Conditions Clarity Enhancement
description: A control measure requiring improvement to Terms and Conditions clarity when systemic fee disputes are identified. This measure ensures that customer-facing documentation is enhanced to reduce misunderstandings.
context: Multiple fee disputes → Improve T&C clarity, better disclosure

name: Fee Disclosure Enhancement
description: A control measure requiring better disclosure of fees to customers when systemic fee disputes are identified. This measure improves transparency and reduces complaint recurrence.
context: Multiple fee disputes → Improve T&C clarity, better disclosure

name: Security Measures Strengthening
description: A control measure requiring the bank to strengthen security measures when systemic fraud complaints are identified. This measure addresses security vulnerabilities revealed through complaint patterns.

name: All Staff
description: All bank staff members are assigned collective responsibilities for complaint handling, including taking complaints seriously, recording them accurately and promptly, escalating appropriately, following procedures, maintaining confidentiality, and treating customers respectfully.

name: Complaints Handling Policy
description: A policy governing the handling of customer complaints by all staff, establishing standards for complaint receipt, recording, escalation, and customer treatment.

name: Mandatory Complaint Recording
description: Staff must record all complaints accurately and promptly upon receipt, ensuring complete documentation of customer grievances.

name: Complaint Escalation Requirement
description: Staff must escalate complaints appropriately according to established procedures, ensuring complaints reach the correct authority or department for resolution.

name: Complaint Confidentiality Obligation
description: Staff must maintain confidentiality regarding all complaint information and customer details disclosed during the complaint process.

name: Respectful Customer Treatment in Complaints
description: Staff must treat customers respectfully throughout the complaint handling process, maintaining professional conduct and dignity.

name: Complaint Procedure Compliance
description: All staff must follow established complaint handling procedures in their interactions with customers and processing of complaints.

name: Serious Complaint Treatment
description: Staff must take all complaints seriously, ensuring no complaint is dismissed or deprioritised regardless of perceived severity.

name: Customer Service and Branch Staff
description: Staff members responsible for receiving customer complaints, providing immediate acknowledgment, logging complaints in the system, and escalating urgent issues to appropriate management.

name: Complaint Receipt and Acknowledgment
description: Customer service and branch staff are required to receive complaints from customers and provide immediate acknowledgment upon receipt.

name: Complaint Logging in System
description: All complaints received must be logged in the system to maintain a record and enable tracking of complaint handling.

name: Escalation of Urgent Issues
description: Customer service and branch staff must escalate urgent issues to appropriate management or designated personnel for priority handling.

name: Complaint Logging System
description: A system used by customer service and branch staff to record and track all complaints received from customers, enabling audit trail and escalation management.

name: Complaints Handler
description: Staff role responsible for investigating customer complaints, documenting findings, following resolution procedures, communicating with customers, meeting regulatory timeframes, and escalating complex cases as needed.

name: Thorough Complaint Investigation
description: Complaints handlers must conduct thorough investigations into all customer complaints received.

name: Complaint Findings Documentation
description: Complaints handlers must document all findings from complaint investigations.

name: Complaint Resolution Procedure Compliance
description: Complaints handlers must follow established resolution procedures when handling customer complaints.

name: Customer Communication on Complaints
description: Complaints handlers must communicate clearly with customers regarding their complaints and resolution status.

name: Complaint Resolution Timeframe Compliance
description: Complaints handlers must meet established regulatory and internal timeframes for complaint resolution.

name: Complaint Escalation
description: Complaints handlers must escalate complaints to appropriate management or specialist teams when necessary.

name: Management
description: Management holds accountability for complaints oversight, including approval of complaints exceeding £2,000, monitoring complaint trends, implementing corrective actions, reporting to the Board, and liaising with external regulators.

name: Board
description: The Board receives complaints reporting and oversight information from Management, including trends, corrective actions, and regulatory liaison matters.

name: Complaints Approval Threshold
description: Management must approve all complaints exceeding £2,000 in value. This provision establishes a financial threshold for escalated approval authority.

name: Complaints Trend Monitoring
description: Management is required to monitor complaints trends to identify patterns, systemic issues, and emerging risks in complaint handling.

name: Corrective Action Implementation
description: Management must implement corrective actions in response to identified complaints trends and issues to prevent recurrence.

name: Board Reporting on Complaints
description: Management is obligated to report complaints matters, trends, and corrective actions to the Board for governance oversight.

name: External Regulatory Liaison
description: Management must maintain liaison with external regulatory authorities regarding complaints and compliance matters.

name: Complaint Handling Policy
description: A policy governing complaint handling procedures across the bank, with mandatory training requirements for all staff levels and specific governance obligations for management and compliance functions.
context: Compliance: FCA rules and reporting requirements

name: Mandatory Annual Complaint Handling Training for All Staff
description: All staff members must complete a 1-hour complaint handling training annually as a mandatory requirement under the complaint handling policy.

name: Enhanced Complaint Handling Training for Customer-Facing Staff
description: Customer-facing staff must complete a 2-hour practical training program including scenarios and role-play exercises annually to ensure competency in complaint handling.
context: Customer-facing staff: 2-hour practical scenarios + role play

name: Management Complaint Governance and Escalation Training
description: Management staff must receive annual training on complaint governance structures and escalation procedures to ensure proper oversight and handling of complaints.

name: Compliance Staff Training on FCA Rules and Reporting Requirements
description: Compliance staff must receive annual training on FCA rules and reporting requirements to ensure the bank meets all regulatory obligations related to complaint handling and reporting.
context: Compliance: FCA rules and reporting requirements

name: All Staff
description: All bank staff members are required to complete mandatory annual complaint handling training to ensure consistent and compliant complaint management across the organization.

name: Customer-Facing Staff
description: Staff with direct customer interaction responsibilities must complete enhanced complaint handling training including practical scenarios and role-play to develop competency in managing customer complaints.
context: Customer-facing staff: 2-hour practical scenarios + role play

name: Management
description: Management is responsible for complaint governance and escalation procedures, requiring annual training to ensure proper oversight and handling of complaints within their areas of responsibility.

name: Compliance
description: The compliance function is responsible for ensuring adherence to FCA rules and managing complaint reporting requirements, requiring annual training on regulatory obligations.
context: Compliance: FCA rules and reporting requirements

name: Financial Conduct Authority Rules
description: FCA regulatory rules governing complaint handling and reporting requirements that the bank must comply with, forming the basis for the complaint handling policy and training obligations.
context: Compliance: FCA rules and reporting requirements

name: Complaint Handling Policy
description: A policy governing the bank's complaint handling procedures, including internal audit requirements, monitoring obligations, and regulatory compliance with FCA standards. The policy establishes frameworks for testing timeliness, compensation appropriateness, and disclosure accuracy.

name: Annual Complaint Handling Testing
description: A mandatory annual internal audit requirement to test the effectiveness and compliance of complaint handling procedures across the bank.

name: Sample File Review for Complaint Handling
